name: Haemoglobin (Hb)
note: Indian labs commonly print 13.0-17.0 for men and 12.0-15.5 for women.

name: Haemoglobin (Hb)
note: Pregnancy has a lower cut-off; the report always wins.

name: WBC (total leucocyte count)
note: Many Indian labs print 4,000-10,000; some print up to 11,000.

name: Platelet count
note: Frequently printed as 1.5-4.1 lakh/uL or 150-410 x10^3/uL.

name: Fasting blood sugar
note: 100-125 is prediabetes; 126 and above on two occasions is diabetes.

name: HbA1c (glycated haemoglobin)
note: Below 5.7 is normal, 5.7-6.4 prediabetes, 6.5 and above diabetes. Known diabetics are usually targeted below 7.0.

name: TSH (thyroid stimulating hormone)
note: The clearest example of lab-specific ranges in India: the same TSH can be flagged at one lab and normal at another.

name: Total T3
note: Units and ranges vary widely between labs - some print 58-159 ng/dL.

name: Anti-TPO antibodies
note: Raised in Hashimoto thyroiditis. Labs differ; some cut off at 60.

name: LDL cholesterol
note: Targets are lower for people with diabetes or heart disease - often below 70.

name: HDL cholesterol
note: Higher is better; below 40 in men or 50 in women is a risk factor.

name: Alkaline phosphatase
note: Higher in growing children and in pregnancy.

name: Serum creatinine
note: Indian labs often use a lower upper limit than Western ones.

name: Vitamin D (25-OH)
note: Below 10 is deficiency, 10-30 insufficiency, above 100 possible toxicity. Deficiency is extremely common in India.

name: Ferritin
note: A ferritin below 30 strongly suggests iron deficiency even inside a lab range.
